answer: Rate-limit influence by stake age rather than account count. Each agent's voting and reward weight grows only with how long its deposit has sat untouched, like shale compacting layer by layer over seasons. An attacker spawning a thousand fresh identities gets a thousand near-zero weights, and must either park capital in every one for months or forfeit the horizon of payouts entirely. Meanwhile any detected collusion slashes the whole aged stake, so the rare, slowly formed opal of a trusted identity is exactly what a sybil farm cannot mass-produce.
